# Here's an unpopular opinion on client gifting: stop sending your own branded swag. | Scrappy ABM · LinkedIn · 2026-08-25

**Scrappy ABM**: Abm is a company that provides account-based marketing plays, podcasts, and chat resources for businesses. They offer a platform for businesses to build repeatable marketing plays, teach how to own them, and graduate their programs. The company focuses on providing a sales team and longer sales cycles for their clients. Scrappy ABM has 10-20 employees, founded in 2023. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, United States. Its workforce is distributed across United States, Argentina, and Colombia.

---

Here's an unpopular opinion on client gifting: stop sending your own branded swag.

We've all done it. A client hits a milestone, so you ship them a box with your logo on a mug, a hoodie, a water bottle. It feels generous.

But here's the thing to sit with: your client doesn't care that much about your business. And that's not an insult. It's just true.

They care about their success. Their goals. Their wins. Not your brand on a t-shirt.

So the way we approach it is simple.

If a client genuinely wants our swag, we absolutely want to give it to them. 🧡💚

But we don't force it as the only option. We send a link where they can opt into our stuff, or pick from plenty of other things they'd actually enjoy.

🔸 If they'd rather have something else, that's there too

Most ecommerce teams talk about the delivery experience as if it’s mainly an operations question: speed, cost, carriers.

Customers don’t really experience it that way.

They experience it as the moment the purchase becomes real. The second they commit, the mindset shifts from browsing to risk. Not dramatic risk, everyday risk: Will this be straightforward? Will anything surprise me? If something changes, will I know what to do?

That feeling isn’t a “nice-to-have”. It behaves like a commercial variable. When lack of clarity arises, customers hesitate, support volume tends to climb, and brand confidence gets quietly chipped away.

# The most expensive automation mistake I see founders make | Mathews Matiiri · LinkedIn · 2026-02-05

**Mathews Matiiri**: Based in United Kingdom [GB].

---

The most expensive automation mistake I see founders make

They see a task that annoys them and throw AI at it.

But annoyance ≠ ROI.

The highest-leverage automation targets aren't the loudest problems — they're the ones leaking the most money:

→ Leads that go cold because follow-up is manual
→ Reports no one builds because it takes 4 hours
→ Proposals that don't get sent because "I'll do it tomorrow"

Before you automate anything, ask:
"What's this costing me per month?"

If you can't answer that, you're guessing.

What's the most expensive manual task in your business right now?
